The authors extend BFNs to handle the periodic nature of crystal structures by operating within a hyper-torus, a space that accommodates the non-additive accuracy dynamics inherent in periodic systems. This adaptation is crucial for accurately modeling the complex interactions within crystals. The method leverages a von Mises distribution for fractional coordinates and a Gaussian distribution for lattice parameters, enabling the model to generate both continuous and discrete crystal properties. A key innovation is the entropy conditioning mechanism, which allows the model to adapt its accuracy based on the entropy of the latent variables, a departure from traditional BFNs that use additive accuracy. The authors also introduce an efficient sampling algorithm that significantly reduces the number of function evaluations (NFEs) required for crystal generation, achieving state-of-the-art performance with only 10 NFEs compared to previous methods that needed thousands. The experimental results demonstrate that CrysBFN achieves superior performance on several benchmark datasets, including Perov-5, Carbon-24, MP-20, and MPTS-52, while also exhibiting significantly improved sampling efficiency. The paper provides a detailed theoretical analysis of the proposed method, including the non-additive accuracy dynamics and the entropy conditioning mechanism. The authors also include ablation studies to validate the importance of each component of CrysBFN, further solidifying the contribution of the work. Overall, this paper presents a significant advancement in the field of crystal structure generation, offering a more efficient and accurate approach than existing methods. The adaptation of BFNs to the periodic domain, coupled with the novel entropy conditioning mechanism and efficient sampling algorithm, represents a substantial leap forward in materials discovery.
